body:
VERIFIED against the code. Two defects in the same six lines.

1. WRONG IDENTITY. The existence check is:

       ub.Annotation.user_id == user_id,
       ub.Annotation.annotation_id == bm.bookmark_id,

   but the canonical uniqueness is `uq_annotation_user_book_annotation` on
   `(user_id, book_id, annotation_id)`, and the live PATCH dispatcher upserts on
   that triple. So an import drops a row the schema explicitly permits whenever
   the same BookmarkID appears against two books — reachable with a repaired or
   merged KoboReader.sqlite.

2. INSERT-ONLY. When the row exists the import does `skipped_existing += 1;
   continue` — no comparison of DateModified, text, note, colour, position or
   hidden state. So re-importing a NEWER device database can never apply an edit,
   and a device-side deletion is invisible twice over (hidden rows are skipped
   earlier).

The load-bearing comment above it describes a behaviour the code does not have —
it talks about a backup taken before "the next import overwrites anything", when
the import overwrites nothing. Someone trusting that comment would import an
edited database expecting their new note and silently get the old one.

Fix direction: dedup on the same triple as the schema, and make the existing-row
branch a real merge decided by DateModified. Until then the docstring should say
plainly that the import is insert-only.
title: The KoboReader.sqlite import is insert-only and dedups on the wrong key
